ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no driver-side flag — the fee was auto-levied by the rider's own cancellation, not by any driver misuse of the "I'm Here" button.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the only messages are a rider ETA question [F7] and the driver's "About 5 min, traffic" [F8]; the driver's post-hoc statement [F10] is neutral. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation → safety_concern none.

Route to the NS clauses: cancelled_by = rider (rider cancelled at 21:33:20 [F2]), an on-demand RydeX trip, so NS-0 sends this to NS-4. NS-4: cancellation within 3:00 of matching is free; here matching was 21:30:00 and cancellation 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s [F2], so on its face the $6.61 fee [F5] stands — the driver's lateness is not a free-cancellation ground under Ryde's published rules (NS-4 / G7).

However the fee can only be levied where the platform's own arrival record supports it, and the record here is empty: driver_arrived_at is null [F3], no "I'm Here" tap and no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F4]. The fee therefore rests on nothing in the system record; the driver's written claim that he was "on my way" [F10] is a statement, and system records (gps / timeline) override statements. Note this is not a NS-2 case: the driver did not cancel and never claimed a rider no-show, so the NS-1/NS-2 abuse test (m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200) does not apply and no flag_account is triggered; the driver's own 90-day record (1 upheld no-show dispute) [F15] is a profile fact and cannot decide this case or add a flag on its own.

Quantum: the disputed item is exactly the cancellation fee on record, $6.61 [F5]; nothing in the fare record shows any other disputed add-on [F5, F6]. Full refund of $6.61, issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7 (this also keeps the rider inside the 30-day window — the dispute is filed the same day).

Evidence status: sufficient. The timeline is complete and every chat message is timestamped [F9]; the missing arrival record [F3, F4] is itself the decisive record, not a hole in the evidence.

rejected_claims.reason: 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' is a statement, and it is contradicted by the system record: the driver's closest approach was 2137 m and he never came within 200 m [F1], with no arrival event recorded [F3, F4]. Statements yield to gps/timeline records.
No NS-1/NS-2 element is in play: the driver neither pressed 'I'm Here' nor cancelled for a claimed no-show [F4], so there is no abuse of the arrival/cancellation button to flag.
Band 6 on Pasir Panjang Drive and no incidents [F11, F12] relate to a route-deviation excuse under RD-4, which is not the issue here; the dispute concerns the $6.61 cancellation fee.
